d: Calculate Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) from shop-floor time and count data or from A, P and Q percentages. Shows the biggest loss factor.
k: OEE Calculator – Availability, Performance, Quality Availability = Run time ÷ Planned production time Run time = Planned production time − Unplanned stop time Performance = (Ideal cycle time × Total units) ÷ Run time Quality = Good units ÷ Total units OEE = Availability × Performance × Quality

d: Calculate takt time from shift length, breaks, shifts per day and customer demand, and check whether your bottleneck cycle time can keep up.
k: Takt Time Calculator – Pace of Production to Demand Available time = (Shift length − Planned breaks) × Shifts per day Takt time = Available time ÷ Customer demand Bottleneck load = Bottleneck cycle time ÷ Takt time

d: Calculate average cycle time and throughput from net production time and units completed. Optionally compare it with takt time.
k: Cycle Time Calculator – Average Time per Unit Average cycle time = Net production time ÷ Units completed Throughput = Units completed ÷ Net production time

d: Calculate production rate in units per hour, compare it with a target rate and see the shortfall or surplus in units.
k: Production Rate Calculator – Units per Hour vs Target Production rate = Units produced ÷ Operating time Attainment = Production rate ÷ Target rate Gap = Target rate × Operating time − Units produced

d: Calculate capacity utilization (actual vs design capacity) and efficiency (actual vs effective capacity) for a plant, line or machine.
k: Capacity Utilization & Efficiency Calculator Utilization = Actual output ÷ Design capacity Efficiency = Actual output ÷ Effective capacity

d: Estimate process lead time from work in process and throughput using Little’s Law, and calculate process cycle efficiency from value-added time.
k: Little’s Law Calculator – Lead Time, WIP & Throughput Lead time = WIP ÷ Throughput Process cycle efficiency = Value-added time ÷ Lead time

t: First Pass Yield & Scrap Rate Calculator
d: Calculate first pass yield (FPY), scrap rate, rework rate and final yield from units entering a process, units passing first time and units scrapped.
k: First Pass Yield Calculator – FPY, Scrap & Rework Rate FPY = Units passing first time ÷ Units entering Scrap rate = Units scrapped ÷ Units entering Rework rate = (Units entering − Passed first time − Scrapped) ÷ Units entering Final yield = (Units entering − Scrapped) ÷ Units entering

d: Calculate DPMO, defects per unit (DPU), process yield and short-term sigma level from defects, units and opportunities per unit.
k: DPMO Calculator – Defects per Million & Sigma Level DPO = Defects ÷ (Units × Opportunities per unit) DPMO = DPO × 1,000,000 DPU = Defects ÷ Units Sigma level = Φ⁻¹(1 − DPO) + 1.5

d: Calculate mean time between failures (MTBF), failure rate and reliability over a mission time for repairable equipment.
k: MTBF Calculator – Mean Time Between Failures MTBF = Total operating time ÷ Number of failures Failure rate λ = 1 ÷ MTBF Reliability R(t) = e^(−t ÷ MTBF)

d: Calculate mean time to repair (MTTR) in hours and minutes, and inherent availability when MTBF is known.
k: MTTR Calculator – Mean Time to Repair MTTR = Total corrective maintenance time ÷ Number of repairs Inherent availability = MTBF ÷ (MTBF + MTTR)

d: Calculate equipment availability from MTBF and MTTR (inherent availability) or from measured uptime and downtime, with equivalent downtime per year.
k: Availability Calculator – From MTBF/MTTR or Uptime Inherent availability = MTBF ÷ (MTBF + MTTR) Achieved availability = Uptime ÷ (Uptime + Downtime) Equivalent downtime per year = (1 − Availability) × 8,760 h

d: Estimate the cost of unplanned downtime from lost output, contribution margin, idle labour and direct repair costs. Get total cost and cost per hour.
k: Downtime Cost Calculator – Cost of Unplanned Stops Lost margin = Downtime × Lost production rate × Contribution margin per unit Idle labour = Downtime × Idle workers × Loaded hourly cost Total cost = Lost margin + Idle labour + Other direct costs

d: Estimate electricity use and cost for a machine or motor from rated power, load, efficiency, operating hours and tariff. Daily, monthly and annual figures.
k: Energy Cost Calculator – kWh & Annual Electricity Cost Electrical input (kW) = Rated power × Load ÷ Efficiency Energy per day (kWh) = Electrical input × Hours per day Annual cost = Energy per day × Operating days × Price per kWh

d: Calculate specific energy consumption (SEC) in kWh per tonne or per unit, and compare it with a baseline to estimate energy saved or over-consumed.
k: Specific Energy Consumption Calculator (kWh/t, EnPI) SEC = Energy consumed ÷ Production output Change vs. baseline = SEC ÷ Baseline SEC − 1 Energy saved = (Baseline SEC − SEC) × Production output

d: Calculate active (kW), apparent (kVA) and reactive (kvar) power from voltage, current and power factor for three-phase or single-phase loads.
k: Three-Phase Power Calculator – kW, kVA & kvar Three-phase apparent power S = √3 × V × I Single-phase apparent power S = V × I Active power P = S × PF Reactive power Q = √(S² − P²)

d: Calculate the capacitor bank rating (kvar) needed to raise power factor from its current value to a target, with the resulting reduction in kVA and current.
k: Power Factor Correction Calculator – Capacitor kvar Qc = P × (tan φ₁ − tan φ₂) φ = arccos(PF) Current reduction = 1 − PF₁ ÷ PF₂

d: Estimate annual kWh and cost savings, and simple payback, from replacing an electric motor with a higher-efficiency model (e.g. IE2 to IE3 or IE4).
k: Motor Efficiency Savings Calculator – IE3/IE4 Payback Output power = Rated output × Load Input power saving = Output × (1 ÷ η_old − 1 ÷ η_new) Annual savings = Input power saving × Hours × Energy price Payback = Installed cost ÷ Annual savings

d: Calculate the reorder point from average daily demand, lead time and safety stock, and check whether your current inventory position means you should order now.
k: Reorder Point Calculator – When to Reorder Stock Lead-time demand = Average daily demand × Lead time Reorder point = Lead-time demand + Safety stock

d: Calculate safety stock for a target service level from demand variability and lead-time variability, using the combined statistical formula.
k: Safety Stock Calculator – Service Level & Lead Time SS = z × √(LT × σd² + d² × σLT²) z = Φ⁻¹(Service level) Reorder point = d × LT + SS

d: Calculate the economic order quantity (EOQ), number of orders per year, order interval and total annual ordering and holding cost.
k: EOQ Calculator – Economic Order Quantity & Total Cost EOQ = √(2 × D × S ÷ H) Orders per year = D ÷ EOQ Total cost = (D ÷ Q) × S + (Q ÷ 2) × H

d: Calculate inventory turnover ratio and days inventory outstanding (DIO) from cost of goods sold and beginning and ending inventory.
k: Inventory Turnover & Days of Inventory Calculator Average inventory = (Beginning + Ending inventory) ÷ 2 Inventory turnover = COGS ÷ Average inventory DIO = Days in period ÷ Inventory turnover

d: Calculate belt conveyor capacity in t/h from load cross-section, belt speed and bulk density, or from load per metre and belt speed.
k: Belt Conveyor Capacity Calculator – Tonnes per Hour Volumetric capacity (m³/h) = 3,600 × A × fill × v Mass capacity (t/h) = Volumetric capacity × ρ Mass capacity (t/h) = 3.6 × q × v

d: Calculate return on investment (ROI), net gain and annualized ROI (CAGR) from investment cost, total return and holding period.
k: ROI Calculator – Return on Investment & Annualized ROI Net gain = Total return − Investment cost ROI = Net gain ÷ Investment cost Annualized ROI = (Total return ÷ Investment cost)^(1 ÷ years) − 1

d: Calculate simple payback period in years and months from initial investment and annual net cash inflow, and check it against useful life.
k: Payback Period Calculator – Years to Recover Investment Payback period = Initial investment ÷ Annual net cash inflow Undiscounted net gain = Annual inflow × Useful life − Investment

d: Calculate break-even volume and revenue from fixed costs, selling price and variable cost per unit, plus the volume needed for a target profit.
k: Break-Even Calculator – Units, Revenue & Margin Contribution margin = Price − Variable cost per unit Break-even units = Fixed costs ÷ Contribution margin Units for target profit = (Fixed costs + Target profit) ÷ Contribution margin

d: Calculate net working hours from start and end times minus unpaid breaks, including overnight shifts, in hours/minutes and decimal hours.
k: Working Hours Calculator – Shift Hours Minus Breaks Shift span = End time − Start time (add 24 h if the shift ends the next day) Net working time = Shift span − Unpaid break

d: Calculate labor productivity as output per labor hour, labor hours per unit and output per worker, and compare with a baseline.
k: Labor Productivity Calculator – Output per Labor Hour Labor hours = Workers × Hours per worker Labor productivity = Output ÷ Labor hours Labor hours per unit = Labor hours ÷ Output

d: Calculate TEEP from OEE, planned production time and calendar time, and see how much capacity the schedule leaves unused.
k: TEEP Calculator – Total Effective Equipment Performance Loading = Planned production time ÷ Calendar time TEEP = OEE × Loading

d: Calculate pump hydraulic power, shaft power and electrical input from flow, head, density and efficiencies, with optional annual energy use.
k: Pump Power Calculator – Hydraulic, Shaft & Input kW Hydraulic power (kW) = ρ × g × Q × H ÷ 1,000 Shaft power = Hydraulic power ÷ Pump efficiency Electrical input = Shaft power ÷ Motor efficiency

d: Estimate power, flow and pressure at a new speed using the fan and pump affinity laws, and the theoretical energy savings from a variable speed drive.
k: Affinity Laws Calculator – VSD Energy Savings Flow₂ / Flow₁ = N₂ / N₁ Head₂ / Head₁ = (N₂ / N₁)² Power₂ / Power₁ = (N₂ / N₁)³

d: Estimate the share of compressor capacity lost to leaks and its annual energy cost using the load/unload test method.
k: Compressed Air Leak Cost Calculator – Load/Unload Test Leakage = Load time ÷ (Load time + Unload time) Energy lost = Compressor power × Leakage × Pressurised hours Cost = Energy lost × Energy price

d: Convert electricity consumption into CO₂-equivalent emissions with your grid emission factor, and calculate emission intensity per tonne or unit of output.
k: Electricity CO2 Emissions Calculator – Scope 2 (kg CO2e) Emissions (kg CO₂e) = Electricity (kWh) × Emission factor (kg CO₂e/kWh) Intensity = Emissions ÷ Production output

d: Calculate net present value, internal rate of return, profitability index and discounted payback for a project with equal annual cash flows.
k: NPV & IRR Calculator – Net Present Value, Discounted Payback NPV = −I + Σ CF ÷ (1 + r)ᵗ + S ÷ (1 + r)ⁿ IRR = the rate r at which NPV = 0 Profitability index = PV of inflows ÷ I

d: Calculate the annual cost of holding inventory from capital, storage, insurance and obsolescence rates, and get the carrying cost rate for EOQ.
k: Inventory Carrying Cost Calculator – Holding Cost Rate Carrying cost rate = Capital % + Storage % + Insurance % + Risk % Annual carrying cost = Average inventory value × Carrying cost rate

d: Calculate the cost per unit from materials, direct labor and overhead for a batch or period, with an optional margin check against selling price.
k: Cost per Unit Calculator – Materials, Labor & Overhead Total cost = Materials + Direct labor + Overhead Cost per unit = Total cost ÷ Good units Margin per unit = Price − Cost per unit
